terms.meaning: India's first empire, ruled from Magadha.
The record of Chandragupta's time by the Greek ambassador Megasthenes. It is lost, known only from extracts.
His moral teaching, inspired by Buddha's compassion, set out in his edicts.
An officer Ashoka appointed to spread these teachings.
The era begun by Kanishka in 78 C.E.
The nomadic Central Asian tribe the Kushans came from.

items.name: Kings of the Mauryan dynasty
items.example: Chandragupta's minister was Vishnugupta, also called Kautilya and Chanakya.

items.name: Arthashastra's discovery and content
items.formula: R. Shamasastry found it in 1902 in Mysore's Oriental Library.
items.example: It covers administration, foreign policy, finance, spies and the military.

items.name: Five city centres of Ashoka's time
items.formula: Pataliputra (capital), Taxila, Ujjain, Kalinga and Suvarnagiri.
items.example: Suvarnagiri was in the Deccan, in modern Karnataka; Taxila was the north-west gateway.

items.name: Battle of Kalinga
items.formula: Eight years after his coronation Ashoka won it: about 150000 captured and 1,00,000 dead.
items.example: The suffering made him regret war and turn to Dhamma.

items.name: Ashoka's edicts
items.formula: Mostly in Prakrit language and Brahmi script. His titles: Devanam Priya and Priyadarshi.
items.example: Rock edicts were found at Brahmagiri in Chitradurga district.

items.name: India's National Emblem
items.formula: Taken from the capital of Ashoka's Sarnath pillar.
items.example: The Dharmachakra is carved on its pedestal.

items.name: Mauryan administration
items.formula: Provinces, a permanent army, spies and many officials.
items.example: Land tax was the main income.

items.name: Kings of the Kushan dynasty
items.formula: Founder Kujalakadphisus, then Vimakadphisus and Kanishka.
items.example: They beat the Sakas and Parthians and settled in Gandhara.

items.name: Kushan coins
items.example: After him they minted mainly gold and copper.

items.name: Kanishka's empire
items.formula: From 78 C.E., capital Purushapura, reaching Sanchi and Banaras.
items.example: It also took in Central Asia, and Mathura was another key town.

items.name: Kanishka and Buddhism
items.formula: Mahayana grew and Gandhara sculpture flourished under him.
items.example: Scholars: Nagarjuna, Aswagosha, Vasumitra. Missionaries went to Central Asia and China.

items.name: First and second Buddhist councils
items.formula: First: Ajatashatru, at Rajgriha, chaired by Mahakasyapa.
items.example: Second: Kalasoka, at Vaishali, chaired by Sabakami.

items.name: Third and fourth Buddhist councils
items.formula: Third: Ashoka, at Pataliputra, chaired by Moggaliputta Tissa.
items.example: Fourth: Kanishka, at Kunadalvana in Kashmir, chaired by Vasumitra.

mistakes.text: Vishnugupta, Kautilya and Chanakya are all the same person.
Kanishka is the most famous Kushan king, but Kujalakadphisus is the founder.
Gandhara art grew under the Kushans, not the Mauryas.
